# Preface: The xv6 Philosophy for Machine Learning Systems {.unnumbered}

## Reading a Working System

A call to `loss.backward()` hides a substantial agreement between pieces of a framework. Forward operations must preserve the information their derivatives need. Backward traversal must visit those operations in the right order and combine contributions when paths meet. The optimizer must receive gradients for the parameters it will update. Knowing the chain rule helps explain the mathematics; reading the implementation explains how the agreement holds during execution.

The xv6 commentary offers a model for teaching such agreements. A reader studies a small working system alongside a text that explains its code and design. TinyTorch adopts that relationship between implementation and commentary for machine learning. The aim is to make an execution path small enough to follow while retaining the interactions that give it meaning.

A reference system earns its place through those interactions. A correct matrix operation is necessary for a layer, but the layer must also expose its parameters. A loss can return the right number while breaking the gradient path. A training loop can run without exceptions while weighting the last batch incorrectly. Following a complete computation reveals obligations that a collection of independent examples would conceal.

## A Reference Built for Explanation

TinyTorch uses NumPy arrays for storage and arithmetic. Its Python code implements tensor operations, layer composition, automatic differentiation, optimization, and training, then uses those mechanisms for image and language models. Later modules investigate measurement, compression, and reuse. This boundary keeps numerical inner loops accessible through NumPy while leaving the framework decisions visible in Python.

The implementation deliberately favors mechanisms that can be inspected. Convolution exposes sliding-window loops. Data loading forms batches synchronously. Quantization demonstrates integer codes and reconstruction, while the Tensor wrapper still stores float32 arrays. These choices determine what an experiment can establish. They also give the production discussions a precise starting point: the chapter can explain which representation or execution strategy would have to change to obtain a different cost.

The current source contains complete instructor solutions. That completeness makes the reference useful for tracing, testing, and comparison. A reader can predict a result before running it, change one operation, or reimplement a function and compare behavior with the reference. The commentary supports each approach without requiring unfinished assignments to stand in for an executable system.

## Who This Book Is For

A reader comfortable with Python and matrix multiplication can begin with the tensor chapter and follow how a forward computation takes shape. Partial derivatives and the chain rule become necessary when the book reaches automatic differentiation. Basic probability supports the loss and sampling chapters. GPU programming and compiler construction are not prerequisites for running the reference implementation.

Students building their first framework and engineers investigating familiar APIs share a useful discipline here: identify the caller, follow the data, and state what must remain true when control returns. The chapters develop that discipline through small traces before asking it to carry a complete training or generation workload. The introduction explains how to read the source and commentary together.
